column2: The largest cost driver in agent API spend: the full conversation history is resent with every API call.
Tool schemas plus workspace files sent with every message, whether or not tools are needed.
A periodic background prompt that checks for pending tasks. By default it goes to the primary model carrying full workspace context.
Sending heartbeats to a free local Ollama model instead of the paid primary model. Heartbeats need almost no reasoning capability.
Its 2,048-token window can be too small for heavy memory logs. Erratic heartbeat replies signal a move to a larger local model.
Matching each task to a free, budget, standard or premium model by complexity instead of sending everything to the most capable one.
Explicitly invoking a lightweight agent profile for known simple tasks and using the default profile otherwise. Recommended because it cannot misfire.
A cheap classifier assigns each incoming message a tier before context assembly. Worth it when routing savings exceed classifier overhead.
Gradual drift toward the premium model from identity-file wording, habitual user requests or tool chain escalation. Investigate if Opus exceeds 10% of turns.
Context size at which older turns are summarized and dropped from active context. The summary is appended to the day's memory log.
Context size at which summarization is forced regardless of conversation state.
For many short, independent interactions, cap the message count instead of relying on token thresholds, so stale topics are not carried forward.
Removing stale history also helps answers, because the model's attention is no longer spread across irrelevant context.
Reuse of the processed form of an identical context prefix across calls. Cached reads bill at roughly 10% of the normal input rate.
Place stable content first and variable content last, in the same order on every call, so the prefix matches byte for byte.
Cache lifetime in seconds. Use 300 for interactive chats and longer values for hourly or overnight batch patterns.
The first write in a TTL window costs 125% of the standard input rate; later reads within the window cost 10%.
Inconsistent prefix order, a timestamp or ID inserted before the prefix, an expired TTL, or editing identity files mid-session.
Stops new processing but keeps state and queues messages; resumes when the limit resets. Suited to daily limits.
Stops processing until someone re-enables it manually. Suited to monthly limits where you want to investigate first.
Sends an alert to the configured channel while processing continues. Suited to soft per-session limits.
A hard limit set in the model provider's console slightly above OpenClaw's own cap. It still fires if OpenClaw's enforcement fails.
A script that counts tokens per workspace file. Run it monthly to catch workspace growth that otherwise goes unnoticed.
A monthly pass that drops stale entries, merges related ones and shortens the rest. MEMORY.md is the main source of workspace bloat.
Sudden spikes usually point to loops or router misconfiguration; slow, steady increases usually point to workspace or MEMORY.md growth.
